newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish official says no change to Iran gas deal.
newsitem.headline: Turkish official says no change to Iran gas deal.

text.p: Turkey's Energy Ministry Undersecretary Ugur Dogan on Friday denied press reports that Turkey was seeking revisions to its 23-year, $23-billion deal to get gas through a pipeline from Iran.
"There are no revisions sought. The project has been prepared meticulously over long years and it is going as scheduled," Dogan told Reuters.
Western and Turkish press reports said recently that Turkey was seeking ways to modify some clauses of the agreement, including one on Turkey's payments for gas purchases.
They said displeasure from the Turkish military over alleged Iranian involvements in sheltering rebel Kurdish guerrillas provided cause for Turkey to revise some terms of the agreement.

According to the agreement signed last August, Turkey would get three billion cubic metres (bcm) of gas from 1998 via a pipeline that is being built from Iran's Tabriz to the Turkish capital Ankara. The amount would rise to 10 bcm by 2005.
